findings.reason: the gate must be word-boundaried or the claim dropped, otherwise the node cannot satisfy its own done-when and would report a blocker on a false positive.
findings.text: §16's done-when asserts `grep -rn '_TAG_RE' reckon/` returns "its definition and its one use inside strip_tags and nothing else", but that pattern already matches `_META_TAG_RE` at reckon/_schema.py:239, 355 and 451 (substring match, not the intended symbol), so the stated result is false at the base

findings.reason: the census must either name this site and require it composed from the owner or exempt it explicitly, as the plan already does for `is_section_identity`, or the one-owner claim the census exists to enforce is already violated at the base.
findings.text: the section-id validity grammar `re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*", section_id)` is a copy of `reckon/_schema.py:127` `_RESOURCE_SEGMENT_RE`, re-spelled inside a block that already imports from `reckon._schema` (the same block imports `SECTION_DECLARATION_ENUM`), and the plan's census of section-spelling regular expressions names six sites and omits this seventh

findings.reason: the gate cannot pass as written and does not measure the thing it names; it must grep the inline expression's own text (`<section\b`), or the node's done-when is unsatisfiable.
findings.text: §17's done-when asserts `grep -c 'section\b' reckon/_store.py` returns zero "because the inline section-open expression is gone", but the measured count at the base is 136: the pattern matches the standalone word "section" throughout docstrings, `OpError` messages and the `insert_section`/`collapse_section` symbols, not the inline `<section\b[^>]*>` expression at line 825 that the section names as the copy of `_SECTION_OPEN_RE` to remove

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — one private HTMLParser read in `reckon/_plan_html.py` is projected through a small named-record interface (`plan_headings`) plus the existing `structured_section_spans`, so section enumeration, identity and extent are answered behind an interface smaller than the machinery it hides; no new module is added and the change reduces walk surface.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan's census of section-spelling grammars names six sites and omits the section-id validity grammar re-spelled in `reckon/_store.py:2534` from `reckon/_schema.py`'s `_RESOURCE_SEGMENT_RE`, and §17's own removal gate cannot be satisfied at `reckon/_store.py`.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1477, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §16, §17 and §18 each carry an Interface accounting paragraph that names the added public definitions (`strip_tags`; `plan_headings` and the machinery-element predicate; the schema classification predicate) and states why nothing can be retired, so no section adds surface without accounting for it.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the design names and extends the mechanisms it found (`_StructuredSectionSpanParser`/`structured_section_spans` and `_store`'s collapse helpers in `reckon/_plan_html.py`/`reckon/_store.py`, `routing.section_record_id`, `_schema`'s declaration enum, `interface_counts.read_trees`/`definitions`) rather than adding a parallel reader.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — `strip_tags` is justified as exposing the existing `_TAG_RE` across a package boundary, but the section's done-when tries to prove that singularity with a grep that over-matches another module's `_META_TAG_RE`.
